P1.reason: A lumps the whole game into one group; B separates directions, turn order, disc counting and comparison, though its B1 is still overly broad.

differences.reason: Hurts: one group holding every statement identifies no individual rule at all.
Mixed: covers flanking, placement and flipping, but also lumps in passing, termination and scoring, so it is too broad.
Mostly hurts: number-successor facts plus scan order and counting steps form infrastructure, not one rule.
Helps: board squares, neighbour shifts and emptiness form a clear board-geometry group.
Helps: the eight directions and the step relation cleanly form the line-direction rule.
Helps: per-player disc tally is a coherent counting rule used for winning.
Mixed: the disc placement and flip updates are a fair group, but the initial setup is a separate rule.
Helps: black moves first and turns alternate, a clean turn-order rule.
Helps: the fewer-than comparison is a small, clear helper for deciding who has more discs.
